label: early original-phase steps with certain tokens after c/1/j/y/t (weak, conjunctive token code)
explanation: Sparse (~1% of steps). 74% of activation mass is in the original phase, concentrated at t=2-3 (t=2 alone holds 39%); it never fires at t=0 and almost never at the delimiter. A smaller copy-phase component sits at recall_idx 1 and at the last recall steps of long sequences. Firing is enriched when the current input is v/g/j/u/k/i/b/p and an earlier input (especially the first token) is c, 1, j, y or t. The strongest activations are prefixes like c c v, c 1 v, c c j 3, c c c p. Still, every simple predicate tested (position windows, current token sets, prior-token sets, and their conjunctions) gives dev F1 of 0.22 or less with precision under 0.25, so this looks like a distributed conjunctive code over early-prefix token identities, not a single describable feature. The mass-recall claim was checked; no other magnitude claims were checked.
